outcome: No progress on the stated conjecture (m ≤ n for thrackles) has been found since 26 January 2024; the best bound remains Xu's 1.393(n-1) from 2021, and 2025 work extends thrackle theory to nonplanar surfaces or studies a different (unavoidable-pattern) problem without touching the planar conjecture.
summary: No result changing the status of Conway's thrackle conjecture (that a thrackle on n vertices has at most n edges) was found in the window 26 January 2024 to 22 September 2026. The best known upper bound remains m ≤ 1.393(n-1), due to Xu (2021), which predates the window and was already the recorded state at the time of the frozen Wikipedia revision; no tighter bound, resolution, or counterexample surfaced afterward. Two 2025 papers touch adjacent territory but not the conjecture itself: (1) 'Thrackles on nonplanar surfaces' (arXiv:2506.11808, submitted 13 June 2025) disproves a *different*, generalized conjecture by Cairns and Nikolayevsky about thrackles on genus-g surfaces (m ≤ n + 2g), constructing denser examples (2n + 2g - 8 edges) — this is a related problem posed over different objects (higher-genus surfaces), not a restriction of the planar case, so under §3.1 it is out of scope; the paper explicitly states the original planar conjecture remains unresolved. (2) 'Unavoidable patterns and plane paths in dense topological graphs' (arXiv:2512.04795, submitted 4 December 2025, revised February 2026) studies unavoidable subgraph patterns in dense bipartite topological graphs and plane-path avoidance bounds — a related but distinct extremal topological-graph-theory question that does not reference or bound the thrackle edge count. Wikipedia's own 'Thrackle' article, last substantively updated as recently as 18 May 2026 per its revision history, still cites only the 2021 Xu bound and states the conjecture is open, corroborating that no intervening advance has been recognized by the community. A dedicated tracking page on ProofAtlas (a platform coordinating human/AI research effort on open problems) lists this conjecture as 'open' with 'partial' results depending on literature statements 'that still need independent checking' and explicitly states there is no AI-generated proof or bound for it — the platform organizes tasks but has not itself produced a result. No AI system was found anywhere near this problem. This is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' record: multiple independent, current sources (Wikipedia, ProofAtlas, the two most recent arXiv papers citing thrackles) converge on the same conclusion.
competing_reading: One could argue the nonplanar-surfaces paper (arXiv:2506.11808) is a 'case' rather than a 'variant' if one reads the planar conjecture as the g=0 instance of a general genus-g family. Under that reading the paper would still not settle anything, since it only disproves the *conjectured generalization* for g≥1 and explicitly leaves g=0 (the original) open — so even on the more generous reading, status remains unchanged. I classify it as a related/variant problem (different conjecture, by different authors, over a broader class of surfaces) rather than a restriction of the stated bullet, consistent with the triage's judgment.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement giving a bound on n-vertex planar thrackles better than 1.393(n-1) (progress), an explicit thrackle with more edges than vertices (refutation), or a proof that m ≤ n for all thrackles (resolution) — none of which has appeared as of this search.
